desc_en:
In the end, July leaves too.
July, um... time passed pretty quickly. Honestly there are fewer months that didn't pass quickly for me,
but July passed especially, far too fast.

Personally I'm satisfied and at the same time there is leftover regret
The me from the first semester who was only waiting for summer vacation had a picture of what summer vacation would look like
I don't know from where, and I don't know why, but regret? some kind of leftover longing? remains..

It's no exaggeration to say I spent July quite freely, really like a graduate student
waking up around 10 a.m., heading to the lab or going to the gym
and coming back to the dorm around 3 a.m.?, hanging out a bit, and falling asleep at 4 I think

This is where the problem happened.
Not a sleep problem — what I had set wasn't actually certain.
The dilemma itself every time I woke up was whether to go to the gym first or the lab first

Thinking about it now, it unfolded like this.

Case 1) If I go to the gym first
-> I only have to shower once (after coming back from the gym)

Case 2) If I go to the gym later
-> I have to shower twice

I'll say this in advance.
I am not someone who hates showering, I really hate being dirty and I really hate smelling.
It's nothing else — it's because I think, in that time I could do one more thing..
that's why I have this dilemma, it's absolutely not "ugh I don't want to shower."

While leftover longing and regret remain,
if I check Linear, I've actually gotten quite a lot done.
I was able to study the high school math and science curriculum more deeply and more thoroughly,
and I also got time to recap the OCWs I had already gone through.

Of course research continued through that process too, and fun thoughts kept coming,
and I just wished this kind of life would go on forever...
and in the end the close of July arrived.

From August 15 I have to leave the dorm (I really don't understand this)
so from August 15 until before September 1 I'll basically be studying at home, and I'm more than a little worried.

Ah but. What just occurred to me is that in August there's an autonomous driving special lecture.
The school is hosting it, and students from other schools are coming too,
and I'm looking forward to it and excited, and at times like this I strangely go from ENFJ -> INFJ.

Of course, having said this, once I get close with two or three people I will chatter away with them the whole time.

Thinking about July again, really..
um.... I tried every possible thing to finish 6.1200J properly
and wondered if there was a way to finish CS50x even more perfectly
really... once a little spare room appears, it seems like a person tries every possible thing to fill the empty space.
And still, what keeps remaining in one corner of my mind is... please, just once, I wish someone would give me two weeks. this..

What keeps flickering in my mind is
of course I didn't write the math prettily by hand on a legal pad, and I didn't organize it that well either
I scribbled through it with the thought that I was teaching myself...

What's most regrettable is that I should have organized it in Obsidian each time,
and doing it now the volume is too overwhelming. Starting from polynomials, the first unit of first-year high school math...
I don't yet have the spare room to go all the way through...

And another thing that keeps flickering in my mind..
ah... biology, physics, chemistry too, on the legal pad.. and in Obsidian.. that thought
flickers too.

Of course
science is relatively okay, because looking at the standing of high school science in university science under the 2022 revised curriculum,
it feels closer to an introduction? an entry? and isn't that decisive — I didn't find this out last week,
or three days ago, I found it out just now. Given my personality I'll clearly regret this around three years from now.

But math is different.
Math... I only did first-year high school under the 2022 revision
and the rest, like Math I, meaning the courses from second year, I did all under the 2015 revised curriculum
and that occupies a certain standing in university math.

I think that's really why I can't put my mind at ease so easily.
If it were like science at that level, that feeling would disappear someday,
but math isn't like that.. that's the thought that comes..

Then what I do next is
I talk to myself
"Hey you idiot, if there's overlapping content you can just start writing from the beginning of the university course anyway"

That's the correct answer. That's the optimal solution and the only method.
